CANONICAL_NAME.value: libDAI (0.3 line, 2012 mirror) -- a C++ library of approximate inference on factor graphs: (loopy) belief propagation, junction tree, mean field, TreeEP, Gibbs, and more (Joris Mooij)

VERSION.value: github.com/dbtsai/libDAI master (a 2012 mirror of the libdai.org 0.3 line; exact version from ChangeLog in the tree; commit in hashes)

value.lineage: Pearl's belief propagation (1982/1988) and its loopy generalisation, exact junction-tree inference, and a dozen approximate methods, in one reference library (JMLR MLOSS 2010) with the standard examples (sprinkler network) and unit tests. The canonical open BELIEF-PROPAGATION implementation; the vault's ldpc-codes does BP only for decoding.

value.built_to: compute marginals and MAP states on graphical models by passing messages along factor-graph edges, exactly on trees and approximately on loopy graphs
value.pressure: exact inference is exponential on loopy graphs; loopy BP may not converge
value.success_means: on a tree, BP marginals equal the exact ones; on loopy graphs, convergence and accuracy are reported

value.failure_condition: loopy BP oscillates or converges to wrong marginals

cut.note: loopy belief propagation on a factor graph, cut where libDAI differs from the LDPC decoder in the vault: three message schedules (parallel, sequential random, sequential by maximum residual), a log-domain option, sum-product vs max-product in one code path, and convergence measured on beliefs, not messages

organs.mechanism: for edge (variable i, factor I): multiply the factor by every message into I except the one from i (extrinsic), then sum out (SUMPROD) or max out (MAXPROD) every variable but i, normalise, store as the NEW message (not yet applied); in log domain the product is a sum with the max subtracted before exponentiation; a unary factor short-circuits to its own table
organs.output: a new message (a distribution over i's states)
assumptions: the graph is a tree, or close enough that extrinsic products approximate marginals (the 'loopy' assumption)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the sum-product rule in its general form, one code path for MAP (max) and marginals (sum)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: on loopy graphs messages can oscillate or converge to wrong marginals; libDAI's damping (not read) and the schedules exist because of that

organs.human_name: BP::run (bp.cpp 261-353): PARALL, SEQRND, SEQMAX; findMaxResidual / updateResidual
organs.mechanism: PARALL: compute every new message from the old ones, then apply all (Jacobi); SEQRND: shuffle the edge list each iteration and compute-and-apply edge by edge (Gauss-Seidel in random order); SEQMAX: keep a priority queue of residuals (L-inf distance between a computed new message and the current one), always apply the edge with the largest residual, then recompute the residuals of the messages it influences
organs.state: the residual heap (SEQMAX); the edge permutation
assumptions: on loopy graphs the schedule changes both speed and WHETHER convergence happens; residual scheduling (Elidan, McGraw & Koller 2006) converges where parallel does not
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the same messages under three orders, selectable at run time; the residual schedule is the library's edge over a textbook BP
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: SEQMAX's queue makes each update O(log E); the parallel schedule can oscillate with period 2 on bipartite structures
organs.source_boundary: the schedule branches in run() and the residual helpers

organs.human_name: BP::run: maxDiff over beliefV/beliefF vs _oldBeliefs; props.tol, maxiter, maxtime
organs.mechanism: after each iteration every variable and factor belief is recomputed and compared (L-inf) with the previous iteration's; the largest change is the convergence measure; the loop stops when it falls below tol, or at maxiter, or at maxtime seconds; the final maxDiff is reported (and warned about) either way
assumptions: belief stability is what the user cares about; messages may keep changing in ways that cancel
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a stopping rule on the observable quantity, with three independent budgets
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: recomputing all beliefs per iteration costs as much as an iteration; on oscillation maxDiff never falls and the run ends by budget with a warning, not an error

pressures.condition: the same local message rule as on a tree, but the graph has cycles; the organism chooses the order in which edges are updated; some orders oscillate
pressures.resource_or_constraint: updates per iteration; a residual heap or a random permutation
pressures.failure_condition: no convergence within the budget, or convergence to beliefs far from the exact marginals
pressures.world_punishes: parallel updates on bipartite-like structure; wasted updates on edges that are already settled
pressures.world_rewards: updating where the residual is largest
pressures.observable_consequence: iterations to tol and final belief error vs the junction-tree oracle, per schedule, on graphs with increasing cycle count
pressures.vacuity_condition: a tree (any order converges in one sweep)
pressures.cheat_control: the exact junction tree (in the body) is the ceiling; the parallel schedule on a 4-cycle with strong couplings must oscillate: the world must show both
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: approximate inference on factor graphs (libDAI, Mooij 2010)
